label: lem:segment_pole_sum_uniform_approx
title: Uniform Riemann-sum pole approximation on a segment
statement:
Let \(K \subset \C\) be compact. Let \([a, b] \subset \C\) be an oriented
    line segment whose image is disjoint from \(K\), and let \(g : \C \to \C\)
    be continuous on the segment image. Then for every \(\eps > 0\) there exist
    finitely many sample points \(a_j\) on the segment and coefficients \(c_j\)
    such that
    \[
      \forall z \in K,\qquad
      \left|
        \sum_{j} \frac{c_j}{z - a_j}
        -
        \frac{1}{2\pi i}\int_{a \to b} \frac{g(\zeta)}{\zeta - z}\,d\zeta
      \right| < \eps .
    \]
proof:
The kernel \((\zeta, z) \mapsto g(\zeta)/(\zeta - z)\) is continuous on the
    compact product \(\mathrm{image}([a,b]) \times K\) (the segment image is
    compact and disjoint from \(K\), so the denominator is bounded away from
    zero). Hence it is uniformly continuous, and Riemann sums of the parametric
    integral over a sufficiently fine partition of the unit interval converge
    uniformly in \(z \in K\). Reading off the linear parametrisation
    \(\gamma(t) = a + t(b - a)\) yields sample points on the segment and
    coefficients giving the pole-sum form (after the sign flip
    \(\zeta - z = -(z - \zeta)\) is absorbed into the coefficients).
